ranking.note: Raised from P3: corrects overstated privacy guarantees and adds the experimental designation on a shipping release branch — wrong security/privacy text is the category's top concern; also moved up from position 7.
Moved up from 6: documents limitations/prerequisites of the privatebroadcast privacy feature, the same accuracy concern that drives the two P2 items.
Raised from P4 and moved up from 9: it corrects text that could mislead operators about I2P identity persistence under -privatebroadcast, i.e. wrong privacy documentation, not cosmetics.
Dropped from 2: real value for contributors touching net code, but purely internal developer notes rank below user-facing privacy/behaviour documentation in this category.
Dropped from 3: build/test dependency tables are a convenience consolidation, below documentation whose absence or inaccuracy misleads users about node behaviour.

inconsistencies: #35480 and #35518 are by the same author and both partially close issue #14278 (notification semantics). Review #35518 first: it establishes the general asynchronous/no-ordering contract for -*notify, which #35480 then specialises for ZMQ.

#35858 (new doc/privacy.md) moves privacy guidance out of doc/i2p.md, while #36348 edits doc/i2p.md about -privatebroadcast. These will collide textually; review #35858 first and fold #36348's I2P/persistent-address caveat into it if the sections move.
#36319 is a backport of already-merged #36309 to 31.x — it is not duplicated work, but its content should be checked against master so the master and 31.x privacy wording do not diverge.

#36101 (error-handling strategy) and #30361 (LogError guidance) both edit project-wide developer conventions around errors; if #36101 lands, its terminology for errors vs defects should be reconciled with the LogError wording in #30361.
result.notes: The list clusters into three groups: privatebroadcast/privacy accuracy (#36319, #35858, #36348), external-integration behaviour docs (#35518, #35480), and internal developer/build notes (#36101 excepted, #32278, #35395, #30361). Bands follow that: misleading or missing user-facing security/privacy text first, leverage-bearing design doc alongside it, internal notes last.
